pages.text: The $(item)concrete hose$() works like Create's hose pulley, but pours liquid concrete into rebar.

$(li)Place it above your rebar structure and pipe liquid concrete into its pipe side. It holds $(item)1500 mB$().$(li)Turn it: one direction lowers the hose, the other raises it. The hose stops by itself at the first solid block below it.$(li)$(item)Stop the rotation.$() The hose only pours while it stands still.

Once stopped with at least $(item)1000 mB$() inside, it fills one frame per bucket, starting next to the tip of the hose and spreading $(item)sideways and downwards$(), never up.$(br)It only travels through blocks that can take concrete (rebar frames, industrial pipes, cable tubes, electric posts);

any other block stops the spread, and empty air is never filled.$(br2)So build the whole frame first, connected in one piece, and lower the hose until it rests on top of it. Filled frames then dry into rebar concrete like hand-filled ones.
If rebar is added later next to a finished area, the hose finds it again after a short while without moving it. The reach is the same as Create's hose pulley, set in Create's server config.
